title: MEMTS: Internalizing Domain Knowledge via Parameterized Memory for Retrieval-Free Domain Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models

problem.claim: Time series foundation models often degrade in real-world vertical domains with temporal distribution shifts and domain-specific periodic structures.

gap.claim: Domain-adaptive pretraining can cause catastrophic forgetting, while retrieval-augmented generation introduces substantial retrieval overhead and scalability bottlenecks for real-time stream processing.

contributions.claim: MEMTS is a lightweight, plug-and-play method for retrieval-free domain adaptation in time series forecasting.
Its Knowledge Persistence Module internalizes domain-specific temporal dynamics into learnable latent prototypes and parameterized knowledge representations.
MEMTS compiles retrieved domain knowledge into model parameters for retrieval-free inference without modifying the frozen time series foundation model backbone.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report accurate domain adaptation with constant-time inference, near-zero latency, and mitigation of catastrophic forgetting.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on multiple datasets.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: General-purpose time series foundation models lose performance under vertical-domain shifts and domain-specific periodicity.
Existing adaptation approaches trade off domain fitting, retention of global patterns, and inference efficiency.
MEMTS performs lightweight retrieval-free domain adaptation by compiling offline-retrieved knowledge into model parameters.
The Knowledge Persistence Module represents recurring temporal dynamics as compact learnable latent prototypes.
The authors report efficient inference, reduced catastrophic forgetting, state-of-the-art performance, and public code availability.

source_observation.claim: Retrieval is performed offline once per domain, after which the retrieved knowledge is compiled into model parameters.

interpretation.claim: Moving knowledge access from inference time into parameterized state can reduce serving-time retrieval costs.

application.claim: For latency-sensitive streaming systems, consider offline knowledge consolidation when domain information changes more slowly than predictions are served.

exception.claim: This pattern may be unsuitable when relevant knowledge changes rapidly or must remain dynamically retrievable.

source_observation.claim: MEMTS stores domain-specific seasonal patterns and trends in a compact set of learnable latent prototypes while retaining a frozen general backbone.

interpretation.claim: Separating domain-specific memory from general model parameters may help adapt to local structure while limiting interference with broad temporal patterns.

application.claim: Adaptation systems can isolate domain-specific temporal knowledge in parameter-efficient components rather than modifying the full pretrained model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation works across domains with weakly recurring or highly nonstationary patterns.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the offline retrieval procedure or multi-target supervision construction in detail.
The abstract does not quantify inference latency, memory cost, or adaptation cost.
The abstract does not report limitations, domain-change assumptions, or failure cases.
